where_sql_runs.title: You will practice SQL in the Tools panel on the right.
where_sql_runs.bodyMarkdown:
This course gives you a real **SQL workspace**.

[[image:sql_workspace_overview]]

Your basic loop is:

1. write SQL in the editor;
2. click **Run**;
3. inspect the result.

You will use that same loop throughout the course. The queries will become more capable, but the workspace habit stays the same.

sql_editor_basics.title: The dark editor is where you write your SQL.

running_your_first_query.title: Your first query can be tiny and still feel exciting.
running_your_first_query.bodyMarkdown:
Your first query does not need a table. Run this tiny expression:

~~~sql
SELECT 'Workspace online' AS status;
~~~

Then click **Run**.

[[image:first_query_in_workspace]]

You should get one row and one column named `status`.

The point is not to memorize syntax yet. The point is to complete the full cycle once:

> write → run → inspect

reading_query_results.title: Read results by checking the headers first, then the rows.
reading_query_results.bodyMarkdown:
After a query runs, start with the **column headers**, then read the values underneath them.

For example, if a result shows:

| check |
|---|
| connected |

then `check` is the column name and `connected` is the returned value.

Use the **Tables** view when you need to see which tables are available. Use **Results** when you need to inspect the answer from the query you just ran.

The habit is simple:

> do not stop at “the query ran” — read what it returned.
